items.title: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China
items.desc: Megaspeed, the firm owned by ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's former lover Alice Huang, arranged nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese companies between 2024 and 2025, according to the WSJ. Short seller Culper Research estimates Nvidia's actual China revenue share exceeds 20 percent, far above the officially reported 7 percent. The article Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion worth of Nvidia high-performance chip orders for Chinese companies between March 2024 and June 2025, according to documents reviewed by the Wall Street Journal. The company is owned by Alice Huang, the former lover of since-ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . Megaspeed shipped the chips to buyers in China who maintained long-standing business ties with local tech giants, the WSJ reports. The orders covered several hundred thousand chips that the US had sought to keep out of China through export controls. Megaspeed reportedly gained preferential access to scarce AI chips as an Nvidia cloud partner, apparently because it counted Chinese cloud and tech company Alibaba as a major client. Nvidia officially reported $12.4 billion in China revenue over six months, accounting for 7 percent of total revenue. Short-selling firm Culper Research estimates, however, that more than 20 percent of Nvidia's revenue in the last fiscal year came from Chinese customers. A significant share of that China business may have flowed through indirect channels. items.title: Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first, especially in software and customer service
items.desc: Australia's central bank sees early signs that AI is hitting young entry-level workers in highly exposed jobs like software development and customer service. Since ChatGPT launched, job postings and employment among 15- to 24-year-olds in those fields have dropped more sharply than among older workers. Author Mike Major cautions against jumping to conclusions, however, noting that business cycle shifts and remote work trends could also explain the numbers. The article Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first, especially in software and customer service appeared first on Th
items.full: AI has barely displaced any jobs in Australia so far, but young workers entering highly exposed fields like software development are faring worse. An analysis by Mike Major for Australia's central bank (RBA) built a monitoring system that focuses on the areas where effects are likely to appear first, namely entry-level workers and highly AI-exposed occupations such as programming , clerical work, and customer service. According to the analysis , job postings have fallen across all groups since ChatGPT launched in late 2022, with the steepest drop in the highest-exposure group. In that group, workers aged 15 to 24 and young college graduates have weaker employment rates and higher unemployment than older workers. Ad Major cautions against drawing early conclusions, since the study does not establish direct causation and measures only theoretical exposure, not actual use by companies. Post-pandemic shifts in the business cycle or in remote work could also be driving the numbers. According to SEEK data, AI is complementing existing work while also creating new demand for AI skills . Ad An August 2025 Stanford study based on millions of US payroll records found a similar pattern, with employment among 22- to 25-year-olds in AI-exposed occupations down 13 percent in relative terms since late 2022 and nearly 20 percent among young software developers. More experienced workers in the same occupations held steady or gained ground. A March 2026 Anthropic study also found signs of declining hiring among 22- to 25-year-olds in exposed occupations, with job-finding rates down about 14 percent. It found no systematic rise in overall unemployment, however. Theoretical automation potential and actual AI use are far apart, according to the study. Ad Anthropic offers a company-level example. According to an internal review , the share of junior hires in technical roles has fallen from 27 percent to 9 percent since early 2025. In August 2026, AI agents across the company were already logging six times as many hours as human employees. Anthropic concedes that, as an extremely AI-intensive software company, it is a special case. Even so, researchers warn of a "tragedy of the cognitive commons" , in which disappearing junior roles lead to a future shortage of experienced professionals, assuming those professionals are still needed. A large study of 25,000 workers in Denmark confirms the lack of economy-wide impact. Despite a 64 percent AI adoption rate, researchers found no measurable changes in wages or hours worked. Workers saved an average of just 2.8 percent of their working time. Ad A January 2026 analysis of 10.6 million LinkedIn profiles and US unemployment data , however, cautions against blaming the downturn on AI alone. The research team led by Morgan Frank at the University of Pittsburgh found that the problems in exposed occupations started in early 2022, months before ChatGPT launched. Macroeconomic factors like the Fed's shift in interest rate policy or a correction after pandemic-era hiring surges may play a bigger role than previously assumed. items.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health
items.desc: Apple's new app for a study will answer everyday medical questions
items.full: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health Ivan Mehta 5:30 PM PST · November 15, 2026 Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features. Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people. The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months. The new app will allow users to ask health-related questions, as they do with ChatGPT or Claude, with answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. Apple said that the app will try to give simplified answers to everyday medical questions. Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they’ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys. Participants can share data from HealthKit such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results to get more personalized and pointed suggestions from the app. The company said the app can also help prepare participants better for a doctor’s visit, and it will guide users to specific providers for answers related to concerning medical issues. Apple specified that the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won’t be used to train any kind of AI models. The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours. “At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in a statement, adding, “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.” The app is available to download starting today for U.S. users. It’s not clear if Apple wants to release AI-powered answering to its Health app or Siri yet. The potential is huge — earlier this year, OpenAI said users were asking over 300 million health-related queries each week . items.title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market
items.desc: Bharat Semi says it has secured design wins for its AI-enabled sensor technology with companies including General Atomics.
items.full: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market Jagmeet Singh 3:30 PM PST · November 15, 2026 Bharat Semi , an Indian semiconductor startup, has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop AI-enabled image sensors, as it seeks to win customers in the United States and elsewhere. The investment comes as the nearly five-year-old, pre-revenue startup says it has secured design wins with U.S. defense technology company General Atomics and India’s Kaynes Semicon. Its image sensors, however, remain under development, with the startup targeting its initial commercial production in 2027. India has committed billions of dollars to build up a domestic semiconductor industry, with a hope to become an alternative manufacturing hub as U.S. companies look to diversify supply chains beyond China. The country, however, has yet to establish itself as a major chip manufacturing hub. Meanwhile, the AI boom is also giving Indian startups such as Bharat Semi an opportunity to develop specialized chips for global markets. The New Delhi-based startup is developing programmable image sensors that combine image capture, processing, and AI capabilities on a single chip, reducing the need to send visual data to separate processors. The move could cut system costs by at least 70% compared with conventional setups that use a separate image sensor, image signal processor, and a system-on-chip, co-founder Vrinda Kapoor (pictured above, right) said in an interview. “Our aim here is to move from sensors to sense-making solutions,” Kapoor told TechCrunch. Kapoor, a South Park Commons fellow who earlier worked in healthcare technology, co-founded Bharat Semi in late 2021 with Vinayak Dalmia (pictured above, left), the startup’s managing director, who previously worked at McKinsey and in private equity. Its chief technology officer, Boyd Fowler, previously held the same role at image-sensor maker OmniVision. Bharat Semi is targeting smart homes, industrial automation, surveillance, and aerospace. Without disclosing specifics, Kapoor pointed to air conditioners that could detect when a room is empty and adjust automatically and drones that could process visual information — even with the absence of more expensive computing hardware elsewhere in the system. The startup’s first-generation sensors are already in prototyping, while its second-generation sensors, which will incorporate more advanced AI capabilities, are expected to reach the prototype stage by mid-2027, Kapoor said. Moreover, the startup plans to get those newer sensors into customers’ hands by the end of 2027. The all-equity seed round was led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons, and Indus Bridge Ventures, with participation from Valour Capital, Micromax, Gaingels, and individual investors. Bharat Semi, Kapoor said, plans to use the funding to expand its engineering team, complete product development, and bring its sensors to market. Bharat Semi has about 75 employees across India and the U.S., including 10 to 12 in its American operations, which span engineering and business development in Santa Clara. items.title: Anthropic says the key to agent memory is knowing what to forget, not how much to store
items.desc: Anthropic studied how Claude retains knowledge across sessions. Selective notes beat exhaustive archives by a wide margin. In a Pokémon Red test, the newer Claude Fable 5 got four times as far as the older Sonnet 3.7 by keeping just a handful of strategy files instead of more than 400. A "Dreaming" process retroactively corrects faulty memories. The article Anthropic says the key to agent memory is knowing what to forget, not how much to store appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Anthropic studied how Claude retains knowledge across sessions. Its tests show that selective notes outperform exhaustive archives and that having Claude review its own memories after the fact can correct errors. Anyone who works with an AI agent on a project over several days hits a wall fast, because every new session starts from scratch. In a research post, Anthropic describes how Claude is supposed to retain knowledge across sessions while the model stays unchanged. Claude writes notes to a folder that it can read back later. The core problem, according to Anthropic , is selection. Before it knows what comes next, the agent has to decide in the moment what might matter later, so every note is a bet on the future. Ad In an Anthropic test with Pokémon Red, the older Claude Sonnet 3.7 treated everything as potentially important and, across roughly 10,000 game steps, created 413 files in 225 folders, often a separate one for each battle and item it found. Because the game state keeps changing, the archive goes stale fast. At times, the model did nothing but reorganize its notes instead of playing, and it finished with just a single badge. Ad The newer Claude Fable 5 limited its memory to a few files and earned four badges. Fable 5 didn't record information already visible on screen and instead wrote down plans, strategies, and rules it had tested. Anthropic's comparison, however, covers only a single playthrough per model. Anthropic recommends explaining the purpose of memory to Claude and letting the model decide how to use it. In one benchmark, according to Anthropic, rigid instructions such as "only record mistakes" wiped out most of the advantage for stronger models. Older models, by contrast, benefited from clear instructions, such as being told to actually read their notes before every response. Ad The bigger risk comes from faulty notes that the agent blindly trusts later. Dreaming , an idea that builds on research from Letta and UC Berkeley, is designed to address this. Much like the human brain processes experiences during sleep, Claude goes through transcripts of earlier sessions during a break and checks its notes against them. In the Pokémon test, Claude had incorrectly noted which side of a mountain a landmark was on. Relying on that faulty note, Claude fell into the same trap three times, eventually wanted to give up, and missed its goal. After a Dreaming pass, Claude caught the error by checking the note against the transcript and found the right path. Ad According to Anthropic, Dreaming can also organize larger knowledge bases. Claude built a linked wiki from about 350,000 internal documents from Stainless, a software company Anthropic acquired. Dreaming is supposed to generate new pages while fixing gaps, duplicates, and broken links. The payoff was greatest when Claude could combine the wiki with search, so the wiki worked as a complement rather than a replacement. Ad In a separate legal test by Anthropic, a wiki helped most with questions whose answers were spread across multiple documents. items.title: How to Manage Your WordPress Site From Your Phone With AI (Easy Way)
items.desc: Got a plugin update waiting, a typo on a live page, or a post to schedule, and no laptop nearby? The WordPress app and your phone’s browser can handle some of it, but plugin updates, settings, and page edits are hard to do on a…
items.full: Got a plugin update waiting, a typo on a live page, or a post to schedule, and no laptop nearby? The WordPress app and your phone’s browser can handle some of it, but plugin updates, settings, and page edits are hard to do on a small screen. That’s where an AI assistant helps. Once you connect Claude or ChatGPT to your site, you can describe the change in plain English from your phone, and the assistant makes it for you. Anything you can’t undo waits for your approval first. In this guide, we’ll show you how to manage your WordPress site from your phone using the Claude app and the free WPVibe plugin. Setup takes about five minutes, and we’ll also cover when other apps might be a better fit. For full site management, use the Claude app with the free WPVibe plugin . For writing posts and replying to comments, the official WordPress app also works. For anything else, open wp-admin in your phone’s browser. None of these replace a computer for building a new site design from scratch. Note: The WPVibe method works on self-hosted WordPress and on WordPress.com sites with a paid plan, because those plans let you install plugins. Free WordPress.com sites can’t install plugins. On a free site, use the WordPress app below instead. This method is useful when you need to make a change to your WordPress site but don’t have access to a computer. You can simply open Claude on your phone, describe what you want done, and let it handle the task through WPVibe. WPVibe is a WordPress MCP server . It lets your WordPress site connect with an AI assistant like ChatGPT or Claude. Once connected, you can use plain language to manage your WordPress site without leaving the AI chat box. WPVibe’s free plan includes 100 tool calls per day, while the Pro plan offers 500 per day for $99 a year. Each tool call counts as one action Claude sends to your site. You can use the free plans of ChatGPT or Claude for this if you want. The setup below is a one-time job. After that, any chat on your phone can reach your site. Start in your phone’s browser rather than in an app. Open your WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins » Add New , and search for WPVibe . The plugin is free, and it works on self-hosted WordPress and paid WordPress.com plans. For more instructions, see our tutorial on how to install a WordPress plugin . Once you activate it, WordPress shows an authorization screen asking whether you want to let the application connect to your account. Tap the button to approve the connection. WordPress then creates an Application Password, which is a separate password your site makes for one app, so you never hand over your real login. Once that’s done, WPVibe checks the connection and confirms your site by name. Note: We are using Claude in this tutorial, but you can do the same with the ChatGPT app on your phone. Simply click on in-app menu and go to Customize » Plugins and search for WPVibe plugin to install it. Next, install the Claude app on your phone and open Settings » Connectors . A connector is the link that lets an assistant reach another service, in this case your website. WPVibe sits in Claude’s connector directory as ‘WPVibe for WordPress’, so there’s no server address

items.title: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max takes on Opus 5.5, GPT-6, and Kimi K3.1 Pro at much lower prices
items.desc: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max, a new flagship model with 2.4 trillion parameters that activates only 71 billion per token. A hybrid architecture sharply cuts costs on long contexts. Qwen4-Max lands just behind Kimi K3.1 Pro on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, and Alibaba plans to release smaller Qwen4 models as open source. The article Alibaba's Qwen4-Max takes on Opus 5.5, GPT-6, and Kimi K3.1 Pro at much lower prices appeared first on The Decoder .
items.full: Qwen4-Max is Alibaba's answer to Opus 5.5, GPT-6, and Kimi K3.1 Pro. The new flagship pairs a more efficient architecture with much lower prices and targets professional work in industry, science, and finance. The mixture-of-experts model has 2.4 trillion parameters but activates only 71 billion per token, according to the Qwen team. It processes images natively and offers a one-million-token context window. Qwen4-Max debuts the revamped architecture of the Qwen4 series . Instead of relying only on standard attention layers, Alibaba combines two methods. Three layers compress the prior context into a condensed state, and a fourth layer then picks out only the parts that matter. That sharply cuts compute costs on long inputs, since the model no longer has to give every part of the context equal attention. Ad The architecture also adds four parallel connections between model layers, with dynamic gates meant to stabilize the flow of information. An N-gram embedding layer with 328 billion parameters supplies common token sequences as ready-made building blocks. According to Alibaba, training the 2.4-trillion-parameter configuration ran stably. Training loss fell steadily throughout the run with no sudden spikes. Ad Alibaba's internal evaluations measure model quality in bits per byte across knowledge, code, question answering, and STEM. Qwen4-Max-Base scored best among the five checkpoints tested. It improved 5 to 13 percent over Qwen3.8-Max-Base while activating 25 percent fewer parameters per token. The efficiency gains show up in operating costs. Work360 is Alibaba's own benchmark for industrial work tasks across 721 specialized fields. On it, Qwen4-Max uses roughly a quarter to a third fewer tokens than its predecessor to solve the same tasks. On the agent benchmark Terminal-Bench 4.0, token use drops by nearly half. Ad According to Alibaba, the average cost per Work360 task falls 62 percent, from $4.43 to $1.67. The benchmark score climbs from 47.74 to 52.69 at the same time. Results on external benchmarks are mixed. On long-horizon agent tasks like Agents' Last Exam v1.1, Qwen4-Max scores 46.7 points, the best result in the comparison group. It trails Opus 5.5 and the GPT models on Humanity's Last Exam. On HealthBench Professional, it falls behind the GPT models but edges past Opus 5.5. Ad At its highest reasoning setting, Qwen4-Max scores 43 points on the current Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. That's nine more than Qwen3.8-Max and three behind Kimi K3.1 Pro, the top Chinese model at 46 points. The biggest gains over the predecessor come on HLE-Diamond (up 21 points to 45 percent), AA-Omniscience (up 18), and AutomationBench-AA (up 17). Ad Artificial Analysis puts the cost of Qwen4-Max at $3.27 per Intelligence Index task. That's about a third of Qwen3.8-Max's $10.02 and roughly 11 percent less than Kimi K3.1 Pro's $3.68. The savings come from three places. Token prices are 25 percent lower than the predecessor's, cache hits cost 70 percent less, and the model burns through fewer tokens. items.title: Staggering Scroll-Driven Animations with animation-range-start
items.desc: Imagine a CSS karaoke machine that displays a ball bouncing on text that incrementally highlights, based on progress through via speech recognition and running that kind of animation as a single predictable, holistic effect driven by one progress value. Staggering Scroll-Driven Animations with animation-range-start originally handwritten and published with love on CSS-Tricks . You should really get the newsletter as well.
items.full: NVIDIA L4 GPUs. 5-second cold starts. Scale to zero when idle. The other day on the CSS-Tricks Slack channel, Danny Schwartz shared an interesting recent Master.dev article by Ashutosh Biswas on how to stagger CSS scrolling animations using a clever combo of several emergent CSS features and a lot of math, which Ashutosh admits is “a huge formula and can look intimidating.” I’ll agree with Ashutosh there. A heartbreaking work of staggering genius When Danny Slacked the link for the Frontend Masters article, he described it as “CSS on drugs.” Speaking of drugs, I am on heavy prescription painkillers while recovering from a serious injury, so that might not help my current comprehension skills. Nevertheless, after reading Ashutosh’s article a few times, here’s a meme showing how I’d feel using such an elaborate algorithm for something as mundane as staggering the animations of some characters as they scroll into view. Don’t get me wrong. I know the complexity is because Ashutosh is going for a generic solution in which we can connect a “progress value to an animation, scroll progress, or any other input to drive the staggering.” In fact, I can dream up a scenario in which this might be what we want: Imagine a CSS karaoke machine that displays a ball bouncing on text that incrementally highlights, based on the user’s progress through the vocals measured via speech recognition . Running that kind of animation “not as a collection of independently timed objects, but as a single predictable, holistic effect driven by one progress value” might be exactly what the doctor ordered. This would be true because the staggered animations could be interrelated, and the overall animation would be driven by a custom input that’s not built into the browser. But unlike this hypothetical scenario, replacing the passage of time with scroll progress to control animations is already built into modern CSS. I contend that we’d need a better reason to roll our own implementation than the examples Ashutosh gives. How modern CSS solves staggered scrolling animations Ashutosh showcases a scroll-driven use case as “one of those ideal scenarios where the stagger formula shines.” But a red flag that we’re in danger of reinventing something we can get for free is that the spec for scroll-driven animations is cognizant that if we opt to base an animation on scroll progress rather than on time, then, as Ashutosh says, “the animation we are going to achieve is different from traditional ones because we don’t include time in our considerations.” This is no surprise to the creators of scroll timeline, and the MDN docs make Ashutosh’s point in different words when introducing scroll timeline . The docs also point out that animation-delay is only meaningful when we are using the default time-based document timeline . Therefore, animation-delay does not affect scroll-driven animations. But this is why CSS introduced animation-range-start , which allows us to delay a scroll-driven animation relative to scroll progress and not time. So, as esoteric and trippy as the math-heavy approach appears, that could be because we are doing something that should be simple in an unusual way. Let’s
